deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: How many minutes of moderate to vigorous activity a week do Canadian guidelines suggest?
back: At least 150 minutes a week, plus strength twice a week (CSEP, 95%).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: How many strength sessions a week?
back: At least 2, using the major muscle groups (CSEP, 95%).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: Talk test: you can talk but not sing. What intensity?
back: Moderate. Vigorous means only a few words before a breath (70%).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: Name the three engines to train.
back: Heart (walks, hikes), legs (strength), carry (pack on hills).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: When does the weighted pack start in the 12 week plan?
back: Week 5, light, then small steps up. Base first (Tip).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
back: Weeks 4, 8 and 12 (Tip).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: Biggest training pack in week 12 for an 80 kg person?
back: About 16 kg, about 20% of body weight (Tip, REI guideline 70%).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: Your first hunt is in 10 days. What fitness work?
back: Walk most days with hills, boots and socks on, a light pack twice, sleep 7 to 9 hours. No cramming (Tip).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: Who should check with a health professional first?
back: Anyone pregnant, with a medical condition or disability, or with chest pain or dizzy spells. Use the Get Active Questionnaire (95%).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
back: Step up, split squat, goblet squat, hip hinge, plank or carry, calf raise (Tip).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
back: Short steps, soft knees, poles (Tip).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
back: A hot spot. Stop now, cover it, dry socks (Tip).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: MET value for hunting, hiking with hunting gear?
back: 9.5 METs (Compendium 2024, 95%).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: MET value for dragging a carcass?
back: 9.8 METs (Compendium 2024, 95%).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: How do you estimate calories from METs?
back: METs x body weight in kg x hours (85%).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
front: How much sleep do the guidelines suggest?
back: 7 to 9 hours, consistent bed and wake times (95%).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
back: A 2 hour hill hike with your pack, getting up from the ground with the pack, a steady hold after a climb (Tip).

deck: Fitness for hunting: a 12 week plan for hills, packs and long days
back: Heart first, Incline, Legs, Load a little, Sleep.

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
front: What decides pack size: height or torso length?
back: Torso length (REI, 70%).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
front: Torso length runs from where to where?
back: From the bony bump at the base of the neck to a line between your thumbs on top of your hip bones (70%).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
front: Where does the hip belt sit?
back: Centred on top of your hip bones (the iliac crest) (70%).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
front: Strap order when fitting a pack?
back: Hips, shoulders, load lifters, sternum. "Hungry Sheep Like Salt."

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
back: Pull the top of the load close to your back. Snug, not cranked (Tip).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
front: Where do the heaviest items go?
back: Centre of the pack, close to your spine (65%).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
back: Light, bulky things you need least, like a puffy or sleep gear (65%).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
back: Quick items: headlamp, map, first aid, rain shell (65%).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
back: About 10% of body weight (REI, 70%).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
back: No more than about 20% of body weight (REI, 70%).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
front: Sustainable meat load per trip for a fit adult?
back: About 20 to 30 kg on rough ground (Tip).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
front: How does meat ride on a frame pack?
back: High and close to your back, straps cinched, in breathable game bags (Tip).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
front: Five lifting steps (BC Forest Safety Council)?
back: Size it up, firm footing and grip, bend knees and brace, load close and lift with legs, turn with your feet (85%).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
back: Turn with your feet. Never twist at the waist (85%).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
front: Getting up with a heavy pack from the ground?
back: Sit into it, buckle the hip belt, roll to a knee, push up on the front knee, stand (Tip).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
front: Rifle in or on a vehicle with a full attached magazine?
back: Unlawful. No live round in the breech or attached magazine in or on a vehicle (99%, item 28).

deck: Packs and carrying loads: fit, packing order, and safe lifting
back: Liner bag inside, small dry bags for papers and phone, game bags for meat (Tip).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
front: Where do you get the radio channel for a resource road?
back: The sign at the road entry. The sign beats any map (95%).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
front: Kilometre signs going up. What do you call?
back: Up. Numbers falling: down (65%).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
front: The basic radio call, in order?
back: Road name, kilometre, up or down, plus anything the sign asks (65 to 95%).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
front: Do you need a licence for a resource road mobile radio?
back: Yes, a mobile radio licence (ISED); a radio shop programs it (95%).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
front: Do FRS handhelds need a licence?
back: No, FRS radios are on the ISED licence exempt list (85%). They do not reach the trucks (Tip).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
front: No radio on an active haul road?
back: Wait at the start, follow a radio vehicle and pull over when it does; if none comes, go with extreme caution (85%).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
front: Top speed on a resource road with no posted limit?
back: 80 km/h (BC Forest Safety Council, 85%).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
back: Traffic. Slow down, keep right (85%).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
back: A pullout on a straight with clear sight both ways, never on a curve or crest (85%).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
front: ATV on a Forest Service Road needs?
back: A valid driver's licence and at least $200,000 third party liability insurance (99%, synopsis page 9).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
front: Is hunting from a motor vehicle legal?
back: No (99%, item 22).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
back: Stay with the vehicle: shelter, and easier to find (85%).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
back: No (85%). Carry a satellite messenger.

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
back: 1 800 663 5555 or *5555 on a cell (85%, 2017 guide: VERIFY current).

deck: Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
Vehicles, Forest Service Roads and radio use
front: Name, Number, Up or Down is a memory hook for?
back: The resource road radio call.

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
back: Tent, cooking area and food storage about 100 m apart (WildSafeBC, 85%).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
front: Tent upwind or downwind of the kitchen?
back: Upwind, so smell drifts away from where you sleep (Tip).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
back: At least 4 m up and 3 m from the tree (WildSafeBC, 75%).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
front: No lockers at a truck camp?
back: Food in the vehicle trunk or a hard sided RV (85%).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
back: Never. Not even toothpaste (85%).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
back: Cook in clothes other than the ones you sleep in; store them with the food (85%).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
front: Is a carcass an attractant in law?
back: Yes. Leaving one where people are likely to be can be fined up to $50,000 (99%, synopsis page 15).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
back: No larger than 0.5 m high by 0.5 m wide (95%).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
front: What must be at the campfire?
back: Someone watching with a hand tool or 8 L of water, and a fuel break (95%).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
back: Comfort: sleep relaxed. Limit: curled for 8 hours. Extreme: survival only (70%).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
front: Do pad R values add when stacked?
back: Yes, under ASTM F3340 (75%).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
front: Five tricks for a warm night?
back: Eat before bed, pee first, dry layers and a toque, vent the tent, hot water bottle in a sock (Tip).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
front: Propane heater in the tent with the flap open?
back: No. Carbon monoxide still builds up (80%).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
back: Headache, dizziness, nausea, sleepiness: looks like flu. Get out, call 911 (80%).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
front: Where does meat hang in camp?
back: In game bags, in shade, well away from and downwind of tents, where you can see it (Tip).

deck: Hunting camp: base camp setup, sleeping warm, keeping food from bears
back: Bag it high, Eat away, All smells out, Rubbish out.

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
front: Energy per gram of fat, carbohydrate, protein?
back: Fat 9, carbohydrate 4, protein 4 kcal (FAO, 95%).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
front: Calories an hour hiking with hunting gear, 80 kg?
back: About 760 (9.5 METs x 80 kg) (estimate).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
front: How often should you eat on a hunt day?
back: Something every 2 to 3 hours (Tip).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
back: Weigh before, count drinks, weigh after. 1 kg lost is about 1 L (65%).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
back: Pale is good; dark yellow means drink now (60%).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
back: At least 1 minute; 2 minutes above 2,000 m (HealthLink BC, 95%).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
back: 2 drops of household bleach per litre, wait 30 minutes (95%).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
back: Double the bleach and wait 1 to 2 hours (95%).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
front: Most effective way to disinfect water?
back: Boiling (HealthLink BC, 95%).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
front: Why store a bottle upside down in the cold?
back: Ice forms at the bottom first, not in the lid (Tip).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
back: 4 °C to 60 °C. No more than 2 hours (95%).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
back: 4 °C or colder (95%).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
back: No. Synopsis ethics code, page 77 (99%).

deck: Food and water for long hunt days
Food and water for long hunt days
back: Frequent snacks, Upside down bottles, Every stream treated, Look at your pee.

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
front: Six things to agree at the truck?
back: Where each goes, back by time, meeting point, who shoots what, signals, what if someone is late (Tip).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
front: Zone of fire when walking side by side?
back: About 45 degrees straight ahead each. The middle and behind are no shot zones (75%).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
front: A deer runs between you and your partner?
back: Hold fire (75%).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
front: You lose sight of your partner?
back: Muzzles up or down, no shooting, call out (75%).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
front: Is blaze orange required in BC?
back: No (95%). Wear it with a partner anyway (Tip).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
back: Distress, help (BC Search and Rescue Association, 80%).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
front: Flat hand up in your hand code?
back: Stop, freeze (your agreed code, Tip).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
back: A landmark both know, a clock time, a wait window, then the truck as plan B (Tip).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
front: Who cancels the licence for a deer?
back: The person who killed it, immediately, before handling (99%, item 1).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
front: Can your brother use his licence on your deer?
back: No. Using another person's licence is unlawful (99%, item 2).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
front: On a push, where may the stander shoot?
back: Only in a zone that points away from the pusher's line (Tip).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
front: Can you herd deer with an ATV?
back: No. No motor vehicle or mechanical device to herd or harass wildlife (99%, item 25).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
back: Shooter calls it, both watch, both unload, mark two spots, one tracks one watches, walk up together (Tip).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
back: Go to the meeting point and wait the agreed window, then whistle and call (Tip).

deck: Hunting with a partner: plans, signals, safe zones of fire, splitting up and meeting
back: Place to meet, Leave and back times, Arcs of fire, No shot in the middle, Signals.

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect
front: Synopsis ethics: when may you shoot?
back: Only with a clear shot of a vital part. "You can't pull the bullet back." (99%)

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect
back: All reasonable effort to locate, dispatch, retrieve and include it in your bag limit (99%).

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect
front: Killed or wounded wildlife by accident?
back: Report promptly to an officer (99%, item 18).

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect
Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect
back: Legal, Identified, Safe backstop, Tested range, Easy and steady, No doubt.

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect
front: Last light at the timber edge. Lean?

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect

deck: Ethics and fair chase: the hard calls, wounded game, respect
